answer: One concrete defense is costly-collateral bonding: before an agent can transact, it must lock a scarce stake — think a bar of copper, not free-to-mint confetti. Spinning up a thousand sybils then demands a thousand real bonds, draining an attacker like a trek across dunes with no oasis in sight. Honest agents also accrue reputation that deepens to a rich umber over time, so voting weight tracks earned, expensive history rather than raw identity count.
